html:
The Sharanahua are a small Panoan people of the upper Purus River on the border of Peru and Brazil, in Ucayali and Acre. Their name means "good people".

They live by farming manioc and plantains, fishing and hunting, and are close in language and custom to the Yaminawa and the Mastanawa. The Amazon rubber boom around 1900 brought rubber tappers up the Purus, and with them epidemics and debt labour. Their language is now spoken by few: in Brazil only a handful of the few hundred Sharanahua still use it. Their neighbours include the Huni Kuin.
